title: BLR soundness over $\mathbb{Z}_k$
statement:
Let $k \ge 2$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be normalized, so that $f(0) = 0$. Fix a real number $\varepsilon$ with $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear: for every linear function $g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ (one satisfying $g(x+y) = g(x)+g(y)$ for all $x,y$), the fraction of inputs on which $f$ and $g$ disagree is at least $\varepsilon$. Then the acceptance probability of the BLR linearity test, taken over independent uniform $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, obeys
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{\varphi(k)}{k}\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
where $\varphi$ denotes Euler's totient function.
hypotheses_covered: dist(f,g) ≥ ε for every linear g
